body.checked before registration: on round 1's discovery data, the 14 atlas square rules at every odd n from 9 to 59 fit part B's rule
body.decision: a prediction holds when its value is the exact period at every size; the pattern is refuted by any failure
body.engine: atlas2.Exact: engine.Torus's check with a product tree for the proper-divisor tests; before registration it agreed with engine.Torus.check, reason for reason, on 121 values from 120 random round-1 records with n <= 100 and on all 104 values in the 52 round-1 records with a failed check
body.part A: the 34 atlas rules with a law; the law its factorisation picks from Kepler's round-1 proposals, at sizes where rule 90's or rule 150's period differs from the full bound (square 141 to 303; hexagon and triangle even n to 400 for rule 90, to 300 for rule 150), within the law's subset
body.part B: 112 new square rules (shells K8, B4, C4 with N4, D4, A4) and the four atlas square rules without a law; at odd n the period from the factorisation alone: the full bound 2^sord(n) - 1 unless the rule splits completely; P90(n) for factors 1 + u only; P150(n) for 1 + u + u^2 only; the symmetric 1D rule's period for another single factor; no prediction for mixed factors. Sizes: odd 13 to 61 (new rules), and odd 63 to 203 where rule 90's or rule 150's period differs from the full bound
body.pattern: found after round 1's verdict (examples/linear-atlas, factor.py): a rule that splits completely into one-dimensional factors (on the triangle, whose matrix's square does) has a 1D rule's period; one that does not reaches the full bound
body.seen before registration: Three (rule, size) pairs were computed exactly while timing the engine, before this registration, and their outcome was seen: square N4+D4 at 389, hexagon H1+self at 394 and triangle E+VO+VS at 394; each had the full-bound period. 389 is not a test size; the two at 394 are excluded.
body.title: Does a linear rule's factorisation into 1D passes decide its period?
